text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HAARETZ
- Committee of Reform, Conservative and Orthodox rabbis to draft compromise on conversion bill.
- Israel's May consumer price index 0.5 percent.
- Unemployment up in May by 0.9 percent.
- High Court rejects petitions against the government in Bar-On affair.
- Four Israelis wounded in south Lebanon when tank set off roadside charge.
- Pregnant Filipino woman told to leave Israel or prove her marriage to Israeli is not fictitious.
JERUSALEM POST
- Prime Minister planning cabinet shuffle.
- Opposition vows not to let Bar-On affair rest.
- Jerusalem firm launches internet multimedia experience.
- Finance Ministry director-general: Economic reform too slow.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu to decide soon on reform in foreign currency, budget cut, lowering interest rate.
- Sources say woman close to suspect Gregory Lerner may serve as state witness.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Sharp rise in unemployment; inflation down.
- Netanyahu to decide within days if Neeman will return to justice ministry.
- Arafat denies organising unrest in West Bank, Gaza.
GLOBES
- Aides say Netanyahu to decide in coming days on details of new economic plan.
- May consumer price index suprisingly low.
